STRASBOURG ― The Socialists & Democrats and liberal Renew Europe groups in the European Parliament have suspended talks on a centrist coalition deal with the center-right European People’s Party after it teamed up with the far right on a package of green legislation, according to two people familiar with the matter.
The three political families were negotiating a written midterm coalition agreement ― with the S&D and Renew seeking to lock the EPP into working with the center parties after it repeatedly voted through key migration and climate legislation with the far right since the last EU election in 2024.
As part of that deal, the EPP wanted the other two centrist groups to support incumbent Parliament President Roberta Metsola for a third term.
